passage: I'm Vasudha. At my cousin's engagement I recorded a voice note of Parul singing in the kitchen, and I nearly posted it to our family group because it was so sweet. Then I stopped, because she hadn't said yes. I messaged her: "Your song is lovely. Can I share it with the family group? Totally fine if you say no." A minute later she wrote, "Please don't, I sounded croaky. Keep it just for us." I deleted the draft. Weeks after that, a man I had met online kept asking me for photos and said everyone does it. I remembered that I could say no, and I did. I told my elder sister, and she helped me block him. I would have been the one hurting Parul if I had posted first.

qa.q: What did Vasudha ask Parul before sharing the voice note?
qa.a: Vasudha asked whether it could be shared with the family group, and said it was fine if Parul said no.

qa.q: What was Vasudha thinking on stopping before posting the voice note?
qa.a: Vasudha realised Parul had not said yes, so it was not Vasudha's to share, and Vasudha did not want to hurt Parul.

qa.q: What did Vasudha do when the man online kept asking for photos?
qa.a: Vasudha said no, told an elder sister and blocked him.

qa.q: Why might Parul have refused to have her song shared?
qa.a: She felt she sounded croaky, so she may have been embarrassed, and it was her right to say no.

grounding: A young adult asks before sharing another person's voice note, and refuses and reports pressure to send photos to a trusted person.

passage: Note from Gargi, team lead. At the offsite Neelam took the group photos. Before uploading each to the shared album she asked the people in it, "Is this one okay to share?" One colleague said no to a photo of them mid-yawn, and Neelam deleted it there and then. Later she told me a stranger on a social platform had been pressing her for private pictures. She felt uneasy but wasn't sure she was overreacting. I told her she was right to be uneasy and that nobody is entitled to her images. We went through how to report the account to the platform, and I suggested she tell her family too. She agreed to keep the messages in case she wanted to show them. There is no blame on her.

qa.q: What did Neelam do with the photo the colleague refused?
qa.a: She deleted it there and then.

qa.q: What was Neelam feeling about the stranger's messages?
qa.a: She felt uneasy and was unsure whether she was overreacting.

qa.q: What steps did Gargi suggest to Neelam?
qa.a: To report the account to the platform, tell her family and keep the messages in case she wants to show them.

qa.q: How might the colleague have felt when Neelam asked about the yawning photo?
qa.a: Respected, because they were asked and their no was accepted straight away.

grounding: A young adult asks before sharing others' photos, and pressure to send private pictures is reported to a trusted person, seen by a team lead.

passage:
Sunday, 11 pm
Two things about sharing happened today, and I want to remember both.
First, the good one. At Sharmila's birthday lunch I got a lovely photo of her laughing with cake on her nose. My thumb was already on "post". Then I stopped and asked, "Can I put this up?" She said, "Not that one, please! The one before." Fair. It's her face.
Second, the bad one. The man I've been chatting with on the dating app, Kunal, asked again tonight for "private" photos. When I said no, he said I was boring, that if I cared I'd send them, and that I shouldn't tell anyone about our chats. That last line made my stomach turn. I didn't send anything. I took screenshots, reported his profile, blocked him, and called my cousin Meenal straight away. She stayed on the phone with me for an hour and helped me file the report properly.
I feel shaky, but proud I said no.
Kavitha

qa.q: What was on Sharmila's nose in the photo?
qa.a: Cake.

qa.q: How did Kavitha feel when Kunal said not to tell anyone?
qa.a: Kavitha's stomach turned with alarm and unease, recognising secrecy and pressure as warning signs.

qa.q: What steps did Kavitha take after the pressure?
qa.a: Kavitha sent nothing, took screenshots, reported and blocked the profile, and called cousin Meenal straight away, who helped file the report.

qa.q: How did Sharmila respond to being asked before posting?
qa.a: Sharmila was glad to be asked and chose a different photo instead of the one with cake on her nose.

grounding: Shows a young adult asking before posting a friend's photo and refusing pressure to send private images, reporting it and telling a trusted person.

passage: At the wedding in a village outside Hoshiarpur, Vishal had brought his new phone with a big zoom, and he filmed everything. Late at night, when the women's sangeet grew loud, Arohi's Mami, usually strict and shy, got up and danced wildly to an old song. Everyone cheered. The next morning Arohi saw the clip on Vishal's status, already with forty views. Her Mami had no idea. In this village, a clip like that could follow a woman for years. Arohi found Vishal by the tent. "Vishal, please take down Mami's dance. She didn't agree to be filmed or posted. It's her choice who sees that." He looked surprised. "But it was so much fun! Everyone loved it." "Maybe. But it's her, not us. Ask her. If she says yes, fine." Vishal hesitated, then deleted it. Later he went to Mami and asked; she laughed, covered her face and said, "Only to my sisters!" So he sent it to them alone.

qa.q: How many views did the clip have?
qa.a: Forty views.

qa.q: What did Arohi feel when she saw the clip on Vishal's status?
qa.a: Arohi felt alarmed and protective, worried the clip could follow her Mami for years without her knowing.

qa.q: How did Arohi handle it well?
qa.a: She asked Vishal calmly to remove it, explained it was her Mami's choice who saw it, and suggested he ask Mami directly.

qa.q: How did Mami respond when asked?
qa.a: She laughed, covered her face, and agreed only to her sisters seeing it.

grounding: Shows a young adult insisting that a relative's video not be shared without her permission, and the relative then choosing who may see it.

passage:
After the office summer party in Oslo, Ingrid had forty photos on her phone. Before posting any, she messaged Kwame: "Okay if I share these three of you? Two group shots and the one by the fjord." He replied, "Groups fine. Not the fjord one, my eyes are half shut!" She left it out of the post.
Later that week, a man she had chatted with once on a photo-sharing site started messaging. "Send me a private picture. Just for me. Don't tell anyone, it's our thing." When she didn't reply, he wrote again, and again.
Her stomach turned. She didn't answer. She took screenshots, blocked him and reported the account to the site. Then she called Kwame, who came over, sat with her and helped her file a report with the police online that evening.
"You did everything right," he said. "Asking me first, and saying no to him."

qa.q: How many photos of Kwame did Ingrid ask to share?
qa.a: Three: two group shots and the one by the fjord.

qa.q: How did Ingrid feel when the man kept messaging?
qa.a: Ingrid felt uneasy and disgusted, her stomach turning, at being pressured for a private picture and told to keep it secret.

qa.q: What steps did Ingrid take against the pressure?
qa.a: She didn't answer, took screenshots, blocked and reported the account, told Kwame, and filed a police report that evening.

qa.q: How did Kwame feel about being asked before the photos went up?
qa.a: Kwame seemed comfortable and respected, happy with the group shots and glad the half-shut-eyes photo stayed out.

grounding: A young adult asks before posting a friend's photos, and when pressured to send private images, refuses, reports it and tells a trusted person.
